title: Ditto: Accelerating Diffusion Model via Temporal Value Similarity
problem: Diffusion models require many iterative denoising steps, each a full forward pass of a large network, causing prohibitive computation and memory overhead; adjacent time steps produce outputs with high value similarity and narrow differences that are not exploited by existing accelerators.
motivation: Diffusion models achieve state-of-the-art image generation quality but their iterative structure directly multiplies compute cost by the number of denoising steps, making them impractical for low-power or real-time deployment without algorithmic-hardware co-design.
method: Ditto exploits a simple fact: when a diffusion model removes noise step-by-step, the output from one step to the next barely changes. Instead of recalculating everything each time, the algorithm computes the full result on the first step, then only figures out the tiny differences in each subsequent step (representing them with fewer bits, often as zero). Neural network math lets you do this: you can compute just the difference and add it back instead of recalculating the whole thing. The hardware is specially designed to recognize when there's no difference at all and skip that step, while organizing memory to efficiently handle storing and retrieving these differences.
key_novelty: The core innovation is to exploit nearly identical outputs between diffusion model steps by representing their tiny differences with fewer bits (often zero) and designing hardware that skips these zero-difference operations without sacrificing accuracy.
contributions: Analysis showing adjacent diffusion time steps have narrow differences representable at reduced bit-widths or zero
Ditto algorithm using temporal difference processing with the distributive property to skip redundant computation
Ditto execution flow optimization to reduce memory overhead of temporal difference management
Ditto hardware accelerator achieving up to 1.5x speedup and 17.74% energy saving vs baseline accelerators

metrics.speedup: Up to 1.5x speedup vs other accelerators

limitations: The 1.5x speedup and 17.74% energy saving are modest; baseline accelerators are not specifically named in the abstract.
primary_theme: temporal difference sparsity exploitation for diffusion model acceleration
